title: The Pirates of Masca
story: Hidden deep in a steep volcanic ravine on the northwest coast, the village of Masca was once so isolated it could only be reached on foot or by sea. Locals say pirates and smugglers used the narrow gorge — the Barranco de Masca — as a secret hideout, stashing goods in caves along the cliffs while lookouts watched for ships from the village above. Even today, the only way to reach the cove at the bottom is a multi-hour hike down the ravine or a boat from the sea, which is exactly what made it perfect for hiding from the law.

title: The Day Sir Francis Drake Was Turned Away
story: In 1595, the legendary English privateer Sir Francis Drake set sail for the Canary Islands hoping to capture Spanish treasure ships and seize the port of Santa Cruz. But the Spanish had been warned in advance and had reinforced the city's defences. When Drake's fleet arrived, they found the harbour bristling with cannon and the garrison ready. After a failed landing attempt, Drake gave up and sailed on toward the Caribbean — his only major defeat of the campaign, and one locals still mention with a touch of pride.

title: Where Admiral Nelson Lost His Arm
story: Two centuries after Drake's failed attempt, another famous Englishman tried his luck against Santa Cruz: Admiral Horatio Nelson. In July 1797, Nelson led a night assault on the town, but the landing went badly wrong in heavy surf and cannon fire. Nelson himself was hit by grapeshot while stepping ashore and had to have his right arm amputated aboard ship soon after. The British were forced to retreat — but the story has a twist: the Spanish commander treated the wounded British sailors so generously that Nelson later sent a letter of thanks. A cannon said to be from the battle still stands in Santa Cruz's Plaza de España.
